findings.reason: the plan would wire the existing `--batch` token through the existing owner instead of declaring a fourth new selector.
findings.text: §3 proposes a manifest-scoped selector for `sn review` as new surface, but `resolve_batch_token` (`:81`), `load_focus_file` (`:183`) and `expand_focus_tokens` (`:203`) already turn a token such as `west_production_dd_paths` into a validated, expanded scope and already drive `sn run --batch` (`imas_codex/cli/sn.py:2304`) and `sn release --batch` (`:4780`); the plan never names this module.

findings.reason: the author should extend `sources_manifest.py` / add `--batch` to `sn review`, not fork the resolution.
findings.text: the selector duplicates shared infrastructure: manifest loading/validation (`load_sources_file`), token resolution (`resolve_batch_token`) and focus expansion (`expand_focus_tokens`) are owned by one module and reached by `sn run` and `sn release`; a second, review-local resolution path drifts from that one batch identity.

findings.reason: the section must name the merge with the existing `--batch`/`--batch` CLI family or state why it cannot, so the surface does not silently grow.
findings.text: the §3 release-batch selector adds a CLI option to `sn review` (and the already-landed `groups` value) without stating what it retires or merges; the supplied family counts are all 0, so any addition must account for itself, and the section instead only asserts that `--ids`/`--physics-domain` "cannot express" the cohort.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan repairs existing modules (`review/pipeline.py`, `review/enrichment.py`) and wires one target to `harmonize.build_worklist`; it adds no family of shallow wrappers over shared machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3's manifest-scoped release-batch selector re-implements manifest/path resolution whose owner is `imas_codex/standard_names/sources_manifest.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §3 adds a scoped-batch CLI option to `sn review` without naming what it retires or merges, or naming the existing `--batch` selector it could reuse.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites `harmonize.py` as prior art for the grouped target (verified: `build_worklist` at `imas_codex/standard_names/harmonize.py:387`, no `sn harmonize` command exists) but proposes the release-batch selector in §3 without citing `imas_codex/standard_names/sources_manifest.py`, which already resolves a committed manifest token to a scoped set.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `sn review --target groups` is a thin layer over `harmonize.build_worklist`, and §3 states why that machinery cannot be extended in place (docs-only, read-only, no CLI surface) and why it extends rather than forks it.
